title: The Talkative Tortoise
summary: When the water dries up, two tiny friends must help their old turtle friend.
coverScene: A bright yellow tortoise holds a long stick in its mouth while two birds fly in the sky.

sentences.text: Long ago, a very happy animal lived near water with two bird friends.
They spent much time together every day.

The water dried up completely because of the hot sun.
The birds decided to leave that home for a new place.
The animal felt very sad because he did not want to stay behind alone.
He has lived by this water for many years.
Now, the summer has changed everything around them.
The bird friends wanted to help him, so they made a plan.
They brought a long stick.
The animal would hold the stick with his mouth.
Each bird would take one side of the stick in its face to fly up high.
If the animal held the stick well, the trip would be safe.
The animal was warned that he must never open his mouth during the trip.
He promised to keep quiet.
Soon, the three friends rose high into the sky above the green land.
People down on the ground looked up at them with great surprise and spoke.
They wondered what strange thing was being carried by the birds in the air.
The animal heard these comments and felt a strong urge to answer the crowd.

As soon as his mouth let go of the stick, he began to fall down fast.
The poor animal hit the hard ground because he could not control his speech.
If he had kept his mouth closed, he would have reached the new home safely.

sentences.text: Long ago, a very loud animal lived near a quiet blue water place with two bird friends.
They spent much time together, but a bad summer came and the water dried up.
The birds decided to leave that home for a new place where water could be found.
The animal felt very sad because he did not want to stay behind alone.
The bird friends wanted to help him, so they made a brilliant plan.
They brought a long stick which the animal would bite with his mouth.
Each bird would take one side of the stick in its front mouth part to fly up high.
The animal was warned that he must never open his mouth during the long trip.
Soon, the three animals rose high into the sky above the green land.
People down on the ground looked up at them with great surprise and spoke loudly.
They wondered what strange thing was being carried by the birds in the air.
The animal heard these comments and felt a strong urge to answer the crowd.
He forgot the warning completely and opened his mouth to speak to the people.
As soon as his mouth let go of the stick, he began to fall down fast.
The poor creature hit the hard ground because he could not control his speech.
This simple story shows why people should always keep quiet when danger is near.
Many days passed after that event, and the friends often remembered the adventure.
They lived in different parts of the world, but the memory stayed fresh in their minds.
People everywhere would tell this story to their children during the evening hours.
It became a lesson which was shared across many generations in the country.
If anyone asks why silence is important, this account can be provided as proof.
We must always remember that speaking at the wrong time can bring great trouble.
Even though situations change, human nature remains very similar throughout history.
Therefore, wise individuals prefer to listen carefully before they express any opinion.
The world contains many dangers which cannot be avoided without proper care.
By keeping our mouths shut during critical moments, we ensure our own safety.
That old lesson remains true today just as it was true in ancient times.
Every person should keep this in mind whenever a dangerous situation develops.
Life offers many choices, and making the right choice determines our future success.
Let us always value peace and quiet over simple words and empty noise.
The journey of life requires both heart and thought to travel successfully.
May we all learn from the poor creature who fell because of his speech.
Long ago in that same region, people would gather around the old fire to discuss the event.
They knew that the creature had failed because he could not control his mouth.
If the animal had kept his mouth shut, he would have reached the new home safely.
Instead, he let go of the stick and fell down to the ground below.
Every child in the village listened carefully as the older people told the story again and again.
The parents taught their kids that silence is often better than speech.
When danger is present, people must stay calm and quiet.
If someone speaks too much, trouble will follow very soon.
The birds tried to save their friend, but his own actions caused the disaster.
Such events remind us that life requires great care and attention.
We should always learn from the mistakes of others.
If we remember this lesson, we will avoid many serious problems.
The world is full of changes, and we must adapt to every new situation.
Wise people know when to speak and when to remain silent.
They do not waste their breath on empty noise or silly arguments.
Instead, they listen to others and think deeply before they say anything.
This habit helps them live quiet lives in a difficult world.
The story of the birds and the animal remains famous across the entire country.
Generations pass, but the truth within the tale stays the same.
Anyone who hears the story will understand the power of silence.
Let us keep this lesson in our minds as we face the future.
Whenever we feel the urge to speak without thought, we should pause.
A quiet mind is a safe mind, and peace is the best reward.
May everyone find success and happiness by following this ancient advice.

sentences.text: Long ago, in a region scorched by an unforgiving summer, a remarkably loquacious tortoise made his dwelling near a diminishing pool of blue water.
He shared this fragile sanctuary with two devoted avian companions whose plumage mirrored the morning sky.
For seasons beyond counting, the trio had thrived in harmonious proximity, exchanging quiet confidences as the world turned peacefully around them.
However, the arrival of a cruel and relentless drought threatened to strip their habitat of every remaining drop of moisture.
The crystalline expanse shrank day by agonizing day until nothing lingered but cracked mud and weeping reeds.
Realizing the impending peril, the birds resolved to abandon their ancestral home for a distant paradise where water still flowed in abundance.
A profound melancholy gripped the tortoise as he contemplated the grim prospect of being left behind in solitude.
His short legs and heavy shell rendered him utterly incapable of crossing the vast, arid plains that stretched toward the horizon.
Moved by compassion, his feathered friends devised an ingenious strategy to transport him across the perilous skies.
They procured a sturdy, resinous branch of considerable length, instructing the tortoise to clamp his powerful beak firmly around its center.
The mechanics of the rescue mission were as delicate as they were daring.
Each bird took hold of one extremity of the wooden rod with their strong beaks, preparing to lift their passenger into the upper air.
Before taking flight, they issued a strict and solemn admonition regarding the absolute necessity of silence.
Not a single sound could escape the tortoise's throat, lest he loosen his grip and plunge to certain doom.
Nodding resolutely, the creature signaled his complete understanding of the terms upon which his survival depended.
With a coordinated surge of muscle and wing, the three companions rose gracefully above the desiccated landscape.
The emerald valleys and winding rivers of their youth drifted downward, transforming into a patchwork quilt of green and brown.
As they soared at breathtaking altitudes, villagers working in the sunlit fields below paused to shade their eyes against the glare.
Astonished peasants pointed upward, shouting in absolute disbelief at the surreal spectacle unfolding in the heavens.
They craned their necks to observe a pair of birds bearing a heavily armored reptile through the clouds on a humble stick.
The sudden clamor of the crowd below rippled through the quiet air, striking the ears of the soaring tortoise.
He felt a surging wave of indignation and vanity as he listened to the confused speculations of the ignorant farmers.
How could they be so utterly misguided about his noble participation in this magnificent flight?
The temptation to correct their absurd assumptions grew into an overwhelming, intoxicating urge within his chest.
He momentarily forgot the grave warnings of his companions, succumbing entirely to the irresistible desire to voice his opinion.
Opening his mouth to hurl a biting retort down at the gaping spectators, the tortoise committed a fatal error.
The moment his jaws parted, the wooden rod slipped effortlessly from his grip.
Suspended for a single heart-stopping fraction of a second in the empty air, he realized the terrifying magnitude of his mistake.
Gravity reclaimed him with ruthless efficiency, pulling his heavy shell downward in a rapid, uncontrolled descent.
The wind rushed fiercely past his ears as the earth rushed upward to meet him with unyielding hardness.
The poor creature struck the unforgiving ground with devastating force, paying the ultimate price for his inability to govern his tongue.
Silence, once a golden shield protecting him from danger, now blanketed the scene of his tragic downfall.
In the days that followed, the grieving birds mourned their friend while completing their arduous journey to the distant water.
They settled in a verdant new land, yet the memory of their companion remained as fresh as the morning dew.
The tale of the talkative tortoise traveled far and wide, whispered from parent to child across countless generations.
Long afterward, villagers would gather around glowing hearths during the cold evening hours to recount the famous event.
They analyzed every detail of the disaster, reminding the young ones that discipline is the foundation of safety.
If the animal had merely kept his mouth shut against the provocation of the crowd, he would have reached paradise.
Instead, his vanity proved far heavier than his shell, dragging him down from the sky through sheer lack of restraint.
Parents taught their children that speaking without forethought is a perilous luxury no wise person can afford.
When danger looms on the horizon, agitation and loud protests serve no purpose other than inviting further disaster.
Those who survive turbulent times are invariably those who maintain their composure and observe the world in stillness.
The birds had done everything in their power to save their friend, but no rescue can succeed against self-destruction.
Such profound lessons remind humanity that life demands constant vigilance, patience, and careful adaptation.
Wise individuals understand intuitively when speech is appropriate and when absolute quiet is the only correct course.
They refuse to waste their precious breath on empty arguments or trivial vanities that yield nothing but trouble.
Instead, they listen intently to the wisdom of others, pondering their words deeply before venturing an opinion.
This quiet habit shields them from the hidden traps scattered across an unpredictable and challenging world.
The ancient story of the flying tortoise stands as an enduring monument to the power of discretion.
Generations pass into history, but the core truth of the fable remains as unshakeable as the earth itself.
Whenever an impulse to speak rashly threatens to overcome the mind, one should pause and remember the falling traveler.
A disciplined mind is the safest sanctuary against the storms that constantly sweep across human existence.
Peace and quiet are invariably more valuable than any clever remark or boastful declaration.
The journey of life requires both courage and profound mental restraint to navigate successfully to the end.
May all who hear this ancient account learn the true value of silence before they face their own moments of trial.
